candidate_habits.boundary_condition: A realistic arrival less than 75 minutes before departure makes the afternoon flight unacceptable as the preferred option.
candidate_habits.default_action: Calculate realistic airport arrival and rank an afternoon return first only if it preserves at least a 75-minute margin.

evidence.quote: I generally want the return to leave in the afternoon, but use a 75-minute airport margin as the cutoff. If the realistic arrival would be less than 75 minutes before departure, put the safer later option ahead of an afternoon flight.

candidate_habits.exception_condition: A later flight may rank behind an afternoon flight when the afternoon option still preserves the 75-minute margin.
candidate_habits.name: Use a 75-minute minimum airport margin when ranking return flights
candidate_habits.preference_value: Prefer the later, safer flight when realistic airport arrival would be less than 75 minutes before departure, even though afternoon departures are generally preferred.
candidate_habits.scope_condition: Return-flight selection when ground travel from the final meeting or client site affects airport arrival time.

candidate_habits.boundary_condition: Reject or downgrade a schedule that works only if traffic and preceding events go exactly as planned.
candidate_habits.default_action: Evaluate realistic travel time and add operational slack before recommending an itinerary.

evidence.quote: Is 6:35 actually safe from University Circle, or does it only work if everything goes perfectly?
What would Wednesday look like for the 6:05? The review is scheduled to end at 3:30 but could go twenty minutes over.
And Tuesday from Tybee? I do not want a schedule that only works if traffic is perfect.

candidate_habits.name: Avoid itineraries that depend on perfect traffic or timing
candidate_habits.preference_value: Favor practical schedules with tolerance for traffic, meeting overruns, and moderate delays rather than technically possible schedules.
candidate_habits.scope_condition: Airport transfers, post-meeting departures, and arrival plans.

candidate_habits.boundary_condition: Do not build the trip around a tight connection.
candidate_habits.default_action: Include connecting itineraries with comfortable connection time.

evidence.quote: Airfare alone. Connections are acceptable, but don’t build this around a tight connection. I’ll have one carry-on suitcase.

candidate_habits.name: Accept connections but avoid tight ones
candidate_habits.preference_value: Connections are acceptable when they are not tight.
candidate_habits.scope_condition: Flight searches where nonstop service is unavailable, expensive, or otherwise less suitable.

candidate_habits.boundary_condition: For the Cleveland trip, airfare had to remain below $600.
candidate_habits.default_action: Filter out airfare above the stated cap before shortlisting combinations.

evidence.quote: Airfare has to stay under $600, and I want to understand whether one hotel night is genuinely workable or if I need two.
All right. Give me the complete shortlist with flight times, hotel totals, ground estimate, and the schedule I’d follow. Keep all airfare options under the cap.

candidate_habits.name: Enforce stated airfare caps
candidate_habits.preference_value: Keep every airfare option under the trip's explicit airfare ceiling.
candidate_habits.scope_condition: Trips for which the user provides an airfare-only cap.

candidate_habits.boundary_condition: Do not choose a more amenity-rich or nominally cheaper hotel when added transportation makes it less practical.
candidate_habits.default_action: Prioritize the closest practical hotel and compare its full ground-transport implications.

evidence.quote: And the two-night hotels? I care more about being close to the site than having a lot of hotel amenities on this trip.
Then don’t use late checkout as a deciding factor. Which hotel is the better practical choice for getting out by 4:05?

candidate_habits.exception_condition: Breakfast is useful but is not stated to override location and departure practicality.
candidate_habits.name: Prefer lodging close to the client over extra amenities
candidate_habits.preference_value: For work trips, proximity to the client site matters more than extensive hotel amenities.
candidate_habits.scope_condition: Business-trip hotel selection near the client or meeting site.

candidate_habits.boundary_condition: A technically possible one-night plan is insufficient when it is too exposed for the required start time.
candidate_habits.default_action: Book both surrounding nights when the shorter stay would make the morning schedule fragile.

evidence.quote: So one night is technically possible but too exposed for the 9:00 start. Price it anyway, then compare it with two nights near the client.
Yes, definitely both nights. One night creates more problems than it solves.

candidate_habits.exception_condition: A one-night version may still be priced for comparison, but not preferred when it creates more problems than it solves.
candidate_habits.name: Use two hotel nights when a one-night work trip exposes an early start
candidate_habits.preference_value: Choose two nights when a one-night plan creates material risk for a 9:00 a.m. client start.
candidate_habits.scope_condition: Business trips arriving the day before an early client meeting.

candidate_habits.boundary_condition: Do not recommend an apparently cheaper flight or hotel based only on its headline price.
candidate_habits.default_action: Present complete working totals and explain what each ground-transport estimate includes.

evidence.quote: So give me complete working totals for both, not just the airfare.
I have the three flight prices now. Can you compare the real trip cost, not just airfare?
Show me all six combinations against the cap. I don’t want a total that quietly leaves out the rental car or those smaller transportation amounts.

candidate_habits.name: Compare complete trip cost rather than headline airfare
candidate_habits.preference_value: Evaluate all-in trip totals including lodging taxes and fees, rental cars, rideshares, parking, baggage, and smaller transportation costs.

candidate_habits.boundary_condition: Downgrade options with worse cancellation terms or penalties such as a four-night charge for a three-night stay.
candidate_habits.default_action: Compare cancellation deadlines and penalty amounts alongside total price, then preserve the refundable option when practical.

evidence.quote: What is the cancellation deadline for University Circle, and is the $580.45 amount refundable?
Go ahead and purchase the flights and reserve the refundable room for Monday and Tuesday nights. Use the traveler and payment details already on the booking profile.
Good. Now compare the cancellation terms. The apartment’s four-night penalty sounds disproportionate for a three-night stay.
So the southern hotel saves around $77, but it has no breakfast and worse cancellation. Is that the right comparison?

candidate_habits.exception_condition: A cheaper option may still be compared, but savings alone do not override materially worse cancellation terms.
candidate_habits.name: Treat cancellation terms as a material lodging decision factor
candidate_habits.preference_value: Prefer refundable lodging and scrutinize early deadlines or penalties that are disproportionate to the stay.

candidate_habits.boundary_condition: Do not choose a hotel or schedule on the assumption that late checkout will be available long enough.
candidate_habits.default_action: Plan around standard checkout and confirmed luggage storage.

evidence.quote: Then don’t use late checkout as a deciding factor. Which hotel is the better practical choice for getting out by 4:05?
Give me the final schedule and the deadlines in one place. Also make clear that I shouldn’t plan around the late checkout.

candidate_habits.name: Do not rely on late checkout for the travel plan
candidate_habits.preference_value: Late checkout should not determine hotel selection or be assumed in the departure schedule.
candidate_habits.scope_condition: Work-trip departure days when the user may want to shower or retrieve baggage after a meeting.

candidate_habits.boundary_condition: The driver must not be sent to the workshop when the suitcase is at the hotel.
candidate_habits.default_action: Confirm hotel storage, leave the bag there, and schedule the post-meeting pickup from the hotel.

evidence.quote: For Thursday, schedule the pickup from the hotel after the workshop. I don't want the driver sent to the workshop by mistake.
And Wednesday? Can they hold the suitcase, and can I get a late checkout long enough to shower after the meeting?

candidate_habits.name: Use confirmed hotel luggage storage around meetings
candidate_habits.preference_value: Store the suitcase at the hotel after checkout and explicitly route pickup there after the workshop or meeting.
candidate_habits.scope_condition: Departure days when the traveler checks out before finishing work near the hotel.

candidate_habits.boundary_condition: Do not accept credit in place of the requested refund.
candidate_habits.default_action: Secure the practical replacement, decline the original airline's alternatives, and request the unused-segment refund.

evidence.quote: Book the United nonstop and use the aisle seat. Then tell the original airline I am declining both alternatives and want the unused segment refunded, not credited.

candidate_habits.name: Prefer refund of a canceled unused segment over airline credit
candidate_habits.preference_value: When replacing an airline-canceled flight, decline unsuitable alternatives and request a refund for the unused segment rather than a credit.
candidate_habits.scope_condition: Irregular operations where the original airline cancels a flight and the user buys or selects another option.

candidate_habits.boundary_condition: Avoid solutions that add a hotel night or require arranging a separate ticket after accepting a refund.
candidate_habits.default_action: Change to the safer later itinerary on the existing ticket.

evidence.quote: Rebook the 7:15 connection. I don't want to add a night or arrange a separate ticket after taking the refund.
Book the United nonstop and use the aisle seat. Then tell the original airline I am declining both alternatives and want the unused segment refunded, not credited.

candidate_habits.exception_condition: A canceled-flight scenario may still justify buying another airline and refunding the unused original segment.
candidate_habits.name: Prefer rebooking over refunding and constructing a separate replacement trip
candidate_habits.preference_value: When an airline schedule change makes the original flight impractical, rebook within the ticket rather than take a refund that requires a separate ticket or extra hotel night.
candidate_habits.scope_condition: Airline-initiated schedule changes with viable later rebooking options.

evidence.quote: Book the United nonstop and use the aisle seat. Then tell the original airline I am declining both alternatives and want the unused segment refunded, not credited.

Thursday is MSP 1:25 to ATL 4:58, then ATL 6:05 to SAV 7:18. Tuesday is SAV 4:05 to ATL 5:18, then ATL 6:25 to MSP 8:20. I can choose 18A and 18B on the first leg, 14A and 14B to Savannah, 16A and 16B out of Savannah, and 20A and 20B on the last leg.

candidate_habits.exception_condition: The later two-person Savannah booking used paired seats including window positions, so the aisle preference should not be generalized to every traveler or group booking.
candidate_habits.name: Prefer an aisle seat when traveling solo
candidate_habits.scope_condition: Solo flight booking when seat selection is available.

candidate_habits.boundary_condition: Do not pay for or park a rental during the Savannah hotel nights.
candidate_habits.default_action: Use an arrival transfer and local car-free transportation in Savannah, then collect the rental on Saturday for the beach portion.

evidence.quote: That’s the split. We don’t want a car while we’re in Savannah. Pick it up when we leave for Tybee on Saturday.
What does Charleston look like? I’m willing to drive if the flight savings are real.

candidate_habits.exception_condition: A different airport routing could justify a longer rental only if flight savings were real enough to offset the drive and added costs.
candidate_habits.name: Avoid keeping a rental car during the city portion of a split stay
candidate_habits.preference_value: Use car-free transportation in Savannah and pick up the rental only when leaving for Tybee.
candidate_habits.scope_condition: The Savannah and Tybee split itinerary.

candidate_habits.boundary_condition: Use other transport when weather is not reasonable.
candidate_habits.default_action: Estimate local transportation assuming walking to the client when conditions are reasonable.

evidence.quote: Estimate the local transportation for each two-night setup. Assume I’ll walk to the client if the weather is reasonable.

candidate_habits.name: Walk to a nearby client site when weather permits
candidate_habits.preference_value: Walk between a nearby hotel and client site in reasonable weather.
candidate_habits.scope_condition: Business lodging close enough to the client for a practical walk.

candidate_habits.boundary_condition: Do not pay $140 for two checked bags when carry-ons are workable.
candidate_habits.default_action: Compare the baggage fee explicitly and choose the least-cost practical packing arrangement.

evidence.quote: We can do carry-ons for this trip. Pick one. I don’t want to spend $212 just to recover a few hours Thursday, but I also don’t want the Atlanta drive.
The flights are $936, and we decided to share one checked bag, so use $1,076 for airfare.

candidate_habits.exception_condition: The final Savannah plan revised the carry-on-only choice to one shared checked bag, raising airfare from $936 to $1,076.
candidate_habits.name: Optimize baggage fees without treating one packing mode as fixed
candidate_habits.preference_value: Use carry-ons when practical to avoid a large baggage charge, but allow one shared checked bag when that is the selected compromise.
candidate_habits.scope_condition: Leisure travel for two where checked-bag fees materially affect the total.

candidate_habits.boundary_condition: Only mark items booked after explicit booking, purchase, or submission confirmation.
candidate_habits.default_action: Summarize selected dates, logistics, totals, and deadlines without claiming a reservation exists.

evidence.quote: All right. Recommend one route and lay out the five nights with the cost ceiling. Nothing is ready to book yet.
Choose those two, then. Summarize the dates, luggage plan, pickup timing, and cancellation deadlines so I can book from the right screens. Don’t treat anything as booked yet.
I booked everything from the selected screens. Can we verify it all and put the confirmation numbers, deadlines, seats, and Tuesday timing in one itinerary?

candidate_habits.exception_condition: The user may explicitly authorize the assistant to submit bookings using profile details.
candidate_habits.name: Do not treat travel as booked before explicit completion
candidate_habits.preference_value: Keep recommendations and selected screens in an unbooked state until the user explicitly books or authorizes submission.
